content.hook: What would you eat for 3 days without power?

slides.title: What would you eat for *3 days* without power?
slides.body: No-cook food that keeps on a shelf.

slides.title: Start with ready-to-eat *protein*
slides.body: Canned fish, beans or meat. Pull-tab lids help. Add a manual can opener.

slides.title: Add *energy* that keeps
slides.body: Crispbread, crackers, nut butter, nuts, dried fruit, muesli bars.

slides.title: Buy what you *already eat*
slides.body: Familiar food is comforting. Remember babies, pets and special diets.

slides.title: Go easy on *salty* food
slides.body: It makes you thirstier. Store your water right next to it.

content.caption:
What would you eat for 3 days without power? Here's a calm, simple no-cook list.

Ready-to-eat protein: canned fish, beans or meat. Keep a manual can opener.
Energy that keeps: crispbread, crackers, nut butter, nuts, dried fruit.
Foods your family already likes. Think about babies, pets and special diets.
Go easy on salty snacks. They make you thirstier, so keep water close.

Tip: eat from your stock and replace it. Nothing sits there forgetting its date.

Ready72h has a full 72-hour supply checklist (water, food, medicine, cash, communications), based on MSB, BBK and RCB guidance. Pay what you want, from 2 PLN.
